items.title: Jury-scenario: juror stuurt een echte VIC-aankoop
items.prio: P1 (3). This most directly answers 'integrate Visa into the main chain and jury demo'.
items.why:
A Visa judge who triggers a real Airi purchase from the hands-on demo sees VIC as part of Purser's main chain, not a recorded side run.

The juror picks an amount and a merchant from a fixed menu, and Purser routes it:
- **Under the limit:** Airi mandate, then Max taps, then paid.
- **Over the limit:** a Purser proposal, then CFO Face ID, then the Airi tap, then paid.
- **Merchant not allowed:** refused with 0 Airi calls.
- **Terms altered after approval:** refused by the hash check, as in vic-2 D.

Every outcome writes its own run record and shows on the juror's own result card.

It costs one API call per id.

items.title: CFO-beleid naast VIC v2-mandaatregels zetten
items.why:
Visa's public VIC v2 rules match Purser closely:
- **No edits:** an instruction cannot be changed, only cancelled and created again. That is what vic-2 D shows, where altered terms go to NEEDS_REAPPROVAL.
- **Mandate fields:** per-mandate declineThreshold, effectiveUntilTime and preferred merchant.
- **Aggregate limit:** spend is summed per instruction.
- **Purchase types:** HITL vs AUTONOMOUS.

A side-by-side table that cites developer.visa.com shows Purser's design follows Visa's own model. That speaks to a Visa judge without needing any Visa access.
items.proof: A static, sourced mapping table on /visa: Purser field or rule → VIC v2 concept, with the doc URL (concepts.md 'Controls and rules') and the place in Purser's code or run that enforces it (e.g. vic-2 D ↔ 'no endpoint to modify an instruction'). Optionally, a test showing Purser's policy has a field for each VIC mandate field.
items.honesty:
Present it as a comparison with Visa's documented model, not as a VIC implementation.

Do NOT:
- build a request builder or mock server that looks like VIC
- send to or emulate /vacp
- name anything a VIC emulator

Build on v2, not the v1 'update-purchase-instruction' that llms.txt still lists.

items.title: Kaartdata-afhandeling expliciet maken (PCI)
items.why:
The agent receives a PAN-like number, expiry and CVV in a 0600 file, and a headless Chromium types them into Airwallex's hosted page. A payments judge will ask about PCI scope. A clear, tested statement turns a weak spot into a sign of maturity:
- the credential is single-use DPAN
- it never reaches logs or the model context
- the file is deleted after use
- redaction is tested
- 3DS is treated as a decline
items.proof:
Code:
- A short 'card data handling' block on /visa, read from code constants.
- A test asserting the credential file is removed and that no PAN or CVV pattern appears in run records or ledger, reusing scrubText and redactSecrets.
- Pointers to src/airi/credential.ts and hostedCheckout.ts.
items.honesty:
State plainly:
- This is not a network-tokenised checkout.
- A browser types the single-use credential.
- We have no PCI attestation.
- This is what Airi returns to agents today (open question 2).

Do not claim PCI compliance.

items.title: TAP-herkenning + VIC-betaling in één aankoop
items.prio: P3 (11). Only if items 1-5 are done.
items.why:
TAP and VIC are two separate stories today. The pattern Visa pilots with BILL and Billtrust (20 Oct) is a TAP-identified agent paying with an instruction-bound tokenised credential. One flow would show that pattern on our rails:
1. The agent TAP-signs its order at Packwise, our merchant.
2. Visa's reference proxy verifies the signature.
3. Packwise creates an Airwallex hosted checkout for that order.
4. Purser gets the Airi mandate for Packwise and pays with the Airi credential.
items.proof: One run record linking the TAP signature verification (key id, reference-proxy result), the Airi mandate, the Airwallex PaymentIntent and the CFO terms hash, under a single order id.
items.max_needed: An Airi tap. The Airwallex merchant account must allow Packwise checkouts (already ours).
items.honesty:
TAP stays labelled 'not eligible Visa tooling (Visa, 5 Nov)', so this does not count toward the award entry. Packwise stays labelled 'simulated, our merchant'.

- Use the reference proxy unmodified (TAP licence).
- Do not claim registration in Visa's Agentic Directory or VARS.
- Do not claim a BILL partnership. Say only 'same pattern'.

items.title: Visa-tooling check: visa-best-practices skill + MPP-card verkennen
items.why:
Two low-cost checks:
- `npx skills add visa/ai` lets us review Purser's Visa code and wording against Visa's own best-practice skill.
- Visa's MPP card spec (`mpp-card@0.1.8`, HTTP 402) sits next to Purser's existing x402 rail and would show the agent choosing a rail under policy.

MPP is not listed as eligible tooling (only VIC and ICC), so its value for the award is small.
items.proof: Review notes from the skill applied as fixes, in a commit. Optionally, one 402 endpoint with both x402 and MPP card offered, and the agent's rail choice logged.
items.max_needed: None. Ask Visa whether MPP card counts before building it.
items.honesty: With no gateway, mpp-card mocks charges, so label it 'mock gateway, nothing charged'. Do not call it VIC. Keep it off the award entry unless Visa confirms MPP is eligible.

risks: Max is the bottleneck. CFO and cardholder are the same person, so every paid VIC purchase needs his live Airi tap, and over-limit ones also his Face ID. Items 3, 4, 5 and 7 together need about 20-30 taps over 3 days, plus his presence at the jury demo. Schedule his tap sessions in blocks.

Airi live flakiness: vic-1 failed 3 times before it passed (camelCase output, confirm refused, missed taps, duplicate_request). A juror-driven live purchase can fail in front of the jury. Fix the known failure modes first, and have a clearly labelled 'recorded 7 Nov' fallback. Never use a silent stand-in.

Intelligent Commerce Connect access is UNVERIFIED: approval speed and whether the agentic endpoints work for new test accounts are both unknown. Do not let days 2-3 depend on it. Decide go or no-go by day 2 morning.

Naming risk: 'VIC' for the Airi credential has no written Airwallex confirmation, and Visa's 'counts' is not recorded. Until item 2 lands, keep the wording 'Visa Intelligent Commerce through Airwallex's Airi', attributed to Visa's 7 Nov statement.

Emulator risk: anything that builds or validates VIC v2 /vacp requests locally can read as a VIC emulator, which the honesty rules ban. Keep item 9 a sourced comparison table, not running code that imitates Visa.
TAP licence: Visa's product terms forbid modifying the spec or sample code. Our extra layer (Content-Digest, time window) must stay a separate addition, and the reference proxy must stay unmodified.
Scope: Metal and Airwallex demo work compete for the same 3 days. Items 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are the core. Drop 11 and 12 first if time runs short.

web_research.summary:
Visa agentic commerce state, checked 11 Nov 2026. Sources were developer.visa.com docs (read as raw .md), github.com/visa/ai, github.com/visa/trusted-agent-protocol, the npm registry, Visa press releases and corporate.visa.com. Anything that comes from news reports or that I could not open myself is marked UNVERIFIED.

Bottom line for a 3-day hackathon:
(1) The full Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) path is not reachable in 3 days. The sandbox needs a Token Requestor ID (TRID) and app ID from the Visa Token Service (VTS), a Business Identifier from a regional Visa team, mutual TLS certificates, a message-level encryption key pair and a passkey set up with device binding. Visa's own doc says sandbox connectivity "takes approximately 10 business days".
(2) What a team can really run and show, with no Visa approval:
- Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP): RFC 9421 agent signatures, with Visa's open sample code.
- Visa's card spec for MPP and the `mpp-card` SDK: HTTP 402 card charges, mocked automatically outside production. Visa itself positions this next to x402.
- VIC mandate/spending-control semantics, modelled on the documented rules.
- The VIC request shape (`/vacp/v2/credentials-for-instruction`), built field-for-field against the docs and labelled "sandbox-shaped, not sent".
(3) Worth an immediate sign-up attempt: the "Intelligent Commerce Sandbox" on developer.cybersource.com (Visa Acceptance) is a self-serve form. How fast it is approved, and whether the VIC endpoints work there, is UNVERIFIED.
(4) Strongest story for an invoice/payables product: the Visa + BILL + Billtrust live B2B pilot (20 Oct 2026). A TAP-registered payment agent pays approved supplier invoices with tokenized credentials and controls tied to the buyer's approved instruction. That is exactly the Purser pattern, but it is a partner pilot with no public API.

Discrepancy to know: llms.txt and the MCP examples in visa/ai still list v1 tools, including `update-purchase-instruction` (PUT /vacp/v1/instructions/{id}). The current VIC docs are v2 and say "There is no endpoint to modify an existing instruction or mandate": you cancel and create a new one. Build on v2.

Probes I ran (11 Nov):
- `sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp` returns 401 without the encrypted (JWE) token, as expected.
- `sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc` returned HTTP 500 on an MCP `initialize` call, so I could not confirm the documentation MCP server works anonymously.
- `visacli.sh` reset the connection.
- investor.visa.com was blocked by Cloudflare. The BILL pilot details therefore come from Perplexity excerpts of the Visa investor and corporate releases, not from a page I opened.

Firecrawl credits ran out partway through, so the later pages were fetched with curl and Perplexity. Your Firecrawl credits ran out. Daily MCP credits refresh in 15h 32m. Add credits or upgrade to keep going: https://www.firecrawl.dev/billing/s/y0g4MXQa4jqh5afolaRY9cUcg3hHbKqDPBVgzoq7dCQ

items.title: Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) core API: what it is now (v2)
items.why:
What it is: Visa's platform for agents to pay with tokenized Visa credentials under consumer-approved purchase instructions.

The v2 API has 4 calls:
- POST /vacp/v2/credentials-for-instruction: enroll the consumer, create the instruction and its mandates, and return the first credential, all in one call
- POST /vacp/v2/instructions/{id}/credentials
- POST /vacp/v2/instructions/{id}/confirmation
- PUT /vacp/v2/instructions/{id}/cancel

The credential comes back as a signed (JWS) or encrypted (JWE) payload holding a network token, a one-time cryptogram (72-hour life) and an ECI value.

purchaseType is one of PURCHASE_HITL, PURCHASE_AUTONOMOUS or PURCHASE_RECURRING. Conditional 'buy when X happens' purchases are allowed only with AUTONOMOUS, and the consumer must still be notified and approve.

Environments: sandbox.api.visa.com, then cert.api.visa.com, then api.visa.com. Visa must approve each step. The docs say the sandbox is 'Available to all registered developers', but also that 'establishing connectivity takes approximately 10 business days'. Before the first call you need:
- a Visa-issued externalClientId (TRID) and externalAppId from VTS
- a Business Identifier from a regional Visa team
- a tokenId (vProvisionedTokenID) for the consumer's card
- a device-bound Visa Payment Passkey
- a JWE public key onboarded with Visa
- mutual TLS certificates

Going to production also needs VIC participant approval, onboarding to TAP, VTS and Visa Payment Passkey, registration in the Visa Agent Registry Service (VARS), PCI attestation and signed contracts.

Credible hackathon demo: build the exact v2 request (client.agent.agentSignature with an Ed25519 signature and tag='credential-request', assuranceData, mandates, transactionData) and validate it against the documented rules. Show it as 'sandbox-shaped, not sent' unless you actually get credentials. Do not claim VIC sandbox calls without them.

items.title: VIC spending controls for agents (mandates): the concrete, documented rules
items.why:
These are the most reusable part of VIC for a policy engine, and you can mirror them exactly without any Visa access:
- **Mandate fields:** declineThreshold {amount, currency}, effectiveUntilTime, an optional preferred merchant name, and recurringFrequency (YEARLY at most 5 years).
- **One mandate per retrieval:** each credential retrieval uses exactly one mandateId. Visa sums all transactions on the instruction against the decline threshold, and also checks the single amount and the merchant-name match.
- **Limits:** at most 10 mandates per instruction (these can span merchants, e.g. one budget split across two merchants), 50 tokens per consumerId, and 15 cryptograms per token in a rolling 24 hours.
- **No edits:** an instruction cannot be changed. Cancel it and create a new one.
- **Expiry:** instructions expire after 30 days by default (US). Assurance (authentication) data expires with them.
- **Unique references:** every transactionReferenceId must be unique.
- **Restricted merchant categories:** these are declined automatically. The list is in the 'VIC and TAP Client Implementation Guide', which is not public.
- **3-D Secure:** US merchants get 'Program Not Supported' for agentic transactions. In the EU, strong customer authentication goes through Visa Payment Passkey.
- **Agent Provider duties:** the consumer must review the transaction and explicitly approve releasing the token unless Visa grants an exception; send CE3.0 dispute data; non-discriminatory card choice (VDEP).

Hackathon demo: map your CFO policy one-to-one onto mandates (per-agent declineThreshold, expiry, preferred merchant), enforce the aggregate sum, the 15-per-24h cryptogram cap and cancel-to-change, and show a refusal citing the VIC rule.

items.title: Visa MCP server for VIC + visa/ai toolkit (packages, skills, agent demo)
items.why:
VIC MCP server:
- Lives at https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP) and returns 401 without auth.
- Auth is a JWE bearer token: a JWT signed with your own RSA key, encrypted with Visa's key from its JWKS.
- The server handles X-Pay and message-level encryption internally.
- Tools in the published examples: enroll-card, initiate-purchase-instruction, update-purchase-instruction, cancel-purchase-instruction, retrieve-payment-credentials, confirm-transaction-events. These are v1-shaped, so prefer the v2 semantics.

The example .env still needs VIC and VTS API keys and shared secrets, external client and app IDs, message-level encryption certificates and a vProvisionedTokenId. In other words, the same onboarding gate as the direct API.

github.com/visa/ai (MIT, last commit 30 Sep 2026) contains:
- packages @visa/token-manager, @visa/mcp-client and @visa/api-client
- examples for MCP, direct API and the VDP hello-world call
- vic-agent: LangGraph + Next.js, supports Claude or OpenAI; shows VTS tokenization, FIDO device binding and passkey creation, and must run at https://localsongbird.com:8188
- Claude Code skills visa-best-practices (covers VIC, MPP and HTTP 402) and visa-acceptance-best-practices, installed with `npx skills add visa/ai`

A Documentation MCP server is listed at https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc with a get-docs tool. UNVERIFIED that it works: my MCP initialize call got HTTP 500. The llms.txt index at https://sandbox.mcp.visa.com/mcp/doc/llms.txt does load.

items.title: Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP): fully demoable offline with Visa's open sample code
items.why:
What it is: RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures that let a merchant verify a Visa-approved agent.
- **Signature-Input fields:** created, expires, keyid, alg (Ed25519 in the examples), nonce, and tag.
- **Tags:** 'agent-browser-auth' when browsing and 'agent-payer-auth' at checkout.
- **Binding:** the signature covers @authority and @path, so it is tied to that domain and page and cannot be replayed.
- **Optional objects:** an Agentic Consumer Recognition object (Visa ID token as a JWT signed with PS256), a Payment object (card metadata, credentialHash, payload) and a Browsing IOU.
- **Keys:** Visa hosts public keys at a well-known URL, served as JWK from GET /keys?keyID=.

The repo github.com/visa/trusted-agent-protocol (222 stars, last commit 28 Oct 2025) runs locally with no Visa credentials. It has 5 parts: agent-registry on :8001, a FastAPI merchant-backend on :8000, a Node RFC 9421 verifying cdn-proxy on :3002 (with nonce replay check), a React merchant-frontend on :3001, and a Streamlit tap-agent on :8501.

The VIC v2 API reuses the same signature shape in the JSON body, with tag 'credential-request', checked against VARS.

Licence (Product Terms dated 10 Oct 2025): you may use it in production without Visa pre-approval, but only if you implement 'the most current version of the Specification in its entirety in strict conformance'. You may not modify the spec or the sample code, except porting or translating it within your app. Unpermitted changes are assigned to Visa.

Credible demo:
- your agent signs both browser-auth and payer-auth requests
- a merchant or payee endpoint verifies them
- tampering with path or authority fails
- reusing a nonce fails
- an expired signature fails

You cannot claim registration in the real Visa registry or Agentic Directory: that needs onboarding.

items.title: Visa card spec for Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) + mpp-card SDK: HTTP 402 card payments, runnable today
items.why:
Announced 18 Mar 2026 with the Tempo mainnet and Stripe/Tempo's MPP.

What Visa published:
- an open, processor-agnostic card spec: draft-card-charge-00 at paymentauth.org, built on the IETF 'Payment' HTTP auth scheme draft
- the npm package `mpp-card`, v0.1.8, maintained by jbrans-visa

Flow:
1. The server answers 402 with a challenge: amount, currency, accepted card networks, and an RSA public key (encryptionJwk).
2. A credential issuer provisions a network token and cryptogram, encrypted as a JWE.
3. The client retries with an `Authorization: Payment` header.
4. The server decrypts, charges through a gateway (a Visa Acceptance enabler or your own), and returns a Payment-Receipt header.

Hackathon-relevant detail: when `gateway` is omitted and NODE_ENV is not 'production', charges are mocked automatically. With no client `enabler`, a built-in dev mock is used. Built-in enablers are vgsClientEnabler, visaAcceptanceClientEnabler and visaAcceptanceServerEnabler.

Visa explicitly says this complements x402.

Demo: put one API behind both x402 (stablecoin) and the MPP card method. Show the agent picking a rail under policy and producing a receipt, and label the card leg 'mock gateway'. MPP also lists 'Accept x402 payments' and 'Manage spend' pages, worth a look.

items.title: Visa Payment Passkey (VPP) and agentic tokens
items.why:
**Visa Payment Passkey:** a FIDO/WebAuthn passkey for card-not-present payments, one registration usable across Visa acceptance. In VIC it is created through the VTS FIDO SDK (iframe or popup) after device binding:
1. POST /vts/provisionedTokens/{id}/attestation/options: type=AUTHENTICATE first, then REGISTER with reasonCode DEVICE_BINDING
2. POST /vts/provisionedTokens/{id}/deviceBinding with intent=FIDO; the result is APPROVED, CHALLENGE (step-up by SMS, email, banking app, call and so on) or DECLINED
3. Persist assuranceData.identifier and fidoBlob

In VIC requests the result goes into assuranceData with verificationMethod '23' (FIDO2). If passkey setup fails, no purchase instruction may be created unless Visa has approved an exception.

All of this needs VTS onboarding and an issuer-enabled card. There is no public no-credential passkey sandbox (UNVERIFIED that one exists anywhere).

Agentic tokens:
- **Mechanics:** VTS onboarding with tokenRequestorType=AI_AGENT, then PAN enrollment, then a provisioned token; the agent stores only vProvisionedTokenID.
- **June 2026 announcement (press only, no developer API found):** tokens enriched with transaction-type, channel and payer data, plus a 'token assurance signal'.
- **10 Nov 2026:** Visa's VAS president said 'the future of agentic commerce is tokens'.

Credible demo: run your own WebAuthn passkey approval and emit a VIC-shaped assuranceData record from it, labelled 'VPP stand-in, not Visa-issued'. Do not call it a Visa Payment Passkey.

items.title: Recommended 3-day Visa plan (what is honest to claim)
items.why:
**Day 1:**
- Submit the Cybersource Intelligent Commerce Sandbox and Visa Acceptance sandbox sign-ups, and optionally the Visa CLI request.
- Add `npx skills add visa/ai`.
- Pin `mpp-card@0.1.8`.
- Re-check the TAP implementation against the current spec (tags agent-browser-auth and agent-payer-auth, nonce and expiry, /keys JWK retrieval). The licence requires implementing the current spec in full.

**Day 2:**
- VIC mandate layer: per-agent declineThreshold, effectiveUntilTime, preferred merchant, 10-mandate and 15-cryptogram caps, cancel-to-change, HITL/AUTONOMOUS/RECURRING purchase types.
- A VIC v2 request builder with an Ed25519 'credential-request' agentSignature, plus assuranceData from your own WebAuthn approval, shown as 'not sent'.
- An MPP card 402 endpoint (mock gateway) next to x402, so the rail choice is visible.

**Day 3:**
- If the Cybersource sandbox is live, swap the modelled call for a real sandbox call and record it.
- Otherwise, label it clearly.
- Framing line: 'TAP-signed agent + instruction-bound card credential, the pattern Visa is piloting with BILL/Billtrust'.

**Never claim:** VIC sandbox or production transactions, VARS or Agentic Directory registration, Visa-issued passkeys, or Visa partnership.
